chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim narrated from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Muawiya ibn 'Ammar, from Abu Abdillah Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him), from his fathers (peace be upon them), who said:

When the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) had finished his sa'y between al-Safa and al-Marwah, Gabriel (peace be upon him) came to him upon the completion of the sa'y while he was on al-Marwah, and said: 'Indeed, Allah commands you to command the people to release from ihram, except for the one who brought the offering.' So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) turned his face to the people and said: 'O people, this is Gabriel,' and he pointed with his hand behind him, 'He commands me from Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, to command the people to release from ihram, except for the one who brought the offering.'

So he commanded them with what Allah had commanded. A man stood up to him and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, we are going out to Mina with our heads dripping from the women (i.e., having had sexual relations with their wives during ihram).' And others said: 'He commands us to do one thing and he does another.' He said: 'O people, if I had anticipated from my affair what I have now faced, I would have done as the people did, but I have brought the offering, so let the one who brought the offering not release from ihram until the offering reaches its place.'

So the people shortened (their prayers) and released from ihram and made it an Umrah. Suraqah ibn Malik ibn Ju'shum al-Modliji stood up to him and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, is this which you have commanded us to do for this year of ours or for eternity?' He said: 'No, but for eternity until the Day of Judgment,' and he interlaced his fingers.
And Allah revealed in this regard a verse of the Quran: 'So whoever performs Hajj and Umrah together, then whatever offering is easy to obtain.'

key_terms.السَّعْي: The ritual walking between Safa and Marwah
key_terms.الْهَدْي: The sacrificial animal brought by the pilgrim
key_terms.تَمَتَّعَ: To enjoy/perform Tamattu' (combining Umrah and Hajj)
key_terms.سُرَاقَةُ بْنُ مَالِكٍ: A companion who asked about the duration of the ruling
key_terms.يُحِلُّوا: To release from the state of ihram

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for pilgrims who bring an offering during Hajj regarding their ihram status?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* details the Prophet’s (peace be upon him and his family) instruction at Mina to release from ihram, distinguishing between those who performed *Tamattu'* (who release after Umrah) and those who brought the *Had'y* (who remain in ihram until the sacrifice). It highlights the Prophet’s explicit confirmation that this ruling is eternal (*lil-abad*), a point emphasized by Suraqah ibn Malik’s question, and links the practice directly to the revelation of Surah Al-Baqarah 2:196. The narrative also captures the practical context of the Farewell Pilgrimage, where the Prophet clarified the procedure to avoid confusion among the companions regarding the timing of ihram release.
